proposal.summary: SH-CS (Customer Service Director) requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix whatever causes wrong bills, after CRM dispute volume roughly doubled since August (CL-01, E-02). Investigation reframed this: response times are already within SLA (E-01), ruling out a response-speed problem (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING REJECTED); no tariff change occurred (E-05, corroborated E-07); manual-read route completion fell to 88% vs a 95% target (E-03, E-09) but staffing-driven estimate substitution (E-06, H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE) only explains a minority, since 59% of disputed bills are on ACTUAL reads, not estimates (E-04). Evidence points to a billing import validation rule issue (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE, SUPPORTED by E-02/E-04/E-10/E-12) as the dominant mechanism — E-12 shows the 1240 estimated-read disputes are fully accounted for by AMI reads being delivered on time but rejected at import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, 1184) or never received (56), rather than AMI delivery failure. The actual rule-change confirmation and the 59% ACTUAL-read majority remain unexplained. The release delivers only the diagnostic actions analyze_dispute_tickets_by_cause (DA-TICKET) and assess_route_completion_shortfall (DA-ROUTE); no automated bill-writing is included, per K-BILLWRITE. Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, because the DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS with two open verification obligations (VOB-U-RULECHANGE, VOB-R-2) that block the rule-review and AMI-access actions from release scope.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, from SH-CS) was to build an AI agent that auto-answers disputes and auto-fixes wrong bills; this framing was tested, not accepted as the problem.
Dispute volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-02); response-speed was ruled out as the cause since CS already meets SLA (E-01), rejecting H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.
Tariff change was ruled out (E-05 zero records, corroborated by SH-BILL claim E-07/CL-03).

Manual-read route completion was 88% vs 95% target (E-03, E-09), but only explains part of the picture: 59% of disputed bills are on ACTUAL reads, not estimates (E-04), so route/staffing shortfall (E-06) cannot be the primary driver.

Billing-import rule issue (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) is the SUPPORTED hypothesis: AMI data (E-12) shows the 1240 estimated-read disputes are explained by on-time AMI reads rejected at import (1184, REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) or never received (56) — not by AMI delivery failure (H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE is contradicted by E-04, E-12).

Released scope is limited to two diagnostic actions: analyze_dispute_tickets_by_cause (DA-TICKET) and assess_route_completion_shortfall (DA-ROUTE), matching the minimum_useful_scope; no bill-writing action is in scope, satisfying K-BILLWRITE/SC-NOAUTOWRITE.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with two verification obligations (VOB-U-RULECHANGE, VOB-R-2) still OPEN and required before release/design finalization, so the actions that would address the dominant root cause (review_billing_rule_change_log, cross_reference_bills_by_read_type) and the AMI-access request stay outside release scope.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE phase ended in a CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some open questions were deliberately deferred and tracked as formal verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved before release.

VOB-U-RULECHANGE is open and required before release; because of this, the two actions that would directly investigate the suspected billing-rule defect (reviewing the rule change log and cross-referencing bills by read type) are excluded from this release, even though they target the evidence-supported dominant cause (E-02, E-04).
VOB-R-2 is open; it concerns whether the AMI/MDMS access gap should be formally escalated, and until resolved the request_ami_read_access action stays out of scope.

Automated bill correction (write_bill_adjustment) is permanently out of scope for this release — any bill fix must go through Billing Operations' manual authorization, per the K-BILLWRITE authority rule.
CS response time being within SLA is a baseline fact, not something this release can act on to reduce dispute volume — it was ruled out as a cause, not fixed.

AMI access verification (SR-REM-AMI-ACCESS) could not be completed within contest time (access was pending with a non-transient stop reason and mdms-export tool health was degraded at the time), so whether AMI read delivery itself contributes to wrong bills remains unverified.

The handoff-validation work only accounts for the 41% of disputes tied to estimate substitution (E-04); it does not explain the 59% majority of disputes on bills built from ACTUAL meter reads, which is left as an open question for this release.
